Apple is expected as usual this autumn to release the iPhone 18 series in September, but this year's launch will in several ways echo the abnormal circumstances of the iPhone release during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

Ways the iPhone launch event this autumn may differ from Apple's usual practice

Apple has many very successful products, but the iPhone remains its flagship, accounting for a large share of the company's overall revenue.

Apple therefore naturally strives to keep the iPhone launch consistent. By maintaining a stable new-iPhone release schedule, it can better satisfy Wall Street and consumers.

Generally, Apple unveils new iPhones in early September — usually four new models — and makes them all available later in September.

But 2020 was an exception because of COVID-19.

The 2020 autumn iPhone lineup was not unveiled until October, and initially only two of the new models went on sale, with the other two delayed until November.

This year there are rumours that Apple's launch plans may see a similar kind of disruption.

Although an September launch event is still widely expected, Apple may not put all the new iPhone models on sale at the same time.

As in 2020, only two models are likely to be available at first: the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The much-anticipated foldable model, the iPhone Ultra, is expected to be unveiled in September, but rumours suggest its release date may be pushed back slightly, coming perhaps several weeks after the Pro models go on sale.

Apple may also depart from its usual practice in terms of the total number of iPhone models.

If the rumours of the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 being pushed back to spring 2027 are accurate, only three new models will debut this autumn — the smallest autumn iPhone lineup since 2019.

Whether driven by strategy, or by global memory-chip shortages and the challenges of mass-producing an entirely new foldable device, Apple's autumn 2026 launch event may recreate multiple aspects of 2020.

What would you like to see at this autumn's iPhone launch event? Let us know in the comments.
